Environment design sheet for THE ACCIDENT SITE — INTACT VERSION, a tree-lined passage from an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film.

DESIGN: a narrow raised concrete pathway/passage cutting straight through a dense stand of tall trees planted or grown along both sides — roots breaking through cracks at the pathway's edges, canopies arching partially overhead, dappled light filtering through leaves. LIGHT: dappled golden light breaking through the tree canopy in shifting patterns across the concrete, warm and alive; the valley below falls into cooler blue-grey haze with distance, strong contrast between the warm lit passage and the cool depth beneath it.

Environment design sheet for THE LIVING CITY / THE NEIGHBORHOOD, from an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film.

Distinct from @circuito (the monumental, echoing race territory, built for speed and largely emptied of daily life) — this is where people and dinosaurs actually LIVE: a dense, inhabited residential and market district, human-scaled rather than monumental, full of ordinary morning routine.

DESIGN: the same reclaimed-brutalism architectural language as the rest of the world — old concrete towers, exposed floor slabs, vertical forests growing through broken facades — but here every surface shows generations of habitation: patched walls, hand-built balconies and lean-tos clinging to the original structure, laundry lines strung between buildings, potted plants and small hanging gardens on every ledge, cooking smoke rising from ground-floor hearths. Streets are NARROW and winding compared to circuito's wide monumental avenues — human-scale passages just wide enough for foot traffic, market carts, and a dinosaur or two to pass through single-file.

MARKET LEVEL: ground-floor market stalls built from reclaimed metal and wood, awnings and canopies in the same saturated woven fabric language established for the world (turquoise, coral, saffron, violet) — but here patched, mismatched, personal, not the pristine ceremonial banners of the racing world. Vendor carts, stacked goods, hanging dried plants, ceramic wares, hand-painted signage without legible text.

DINOSAUR INTEGRATION: working dinosaurs are woven into the fabric of daily life, not spectacle — a cargo hauler kneeling at a loading dock, a small courier dinosaur tied at a hitching post, a watering trough built into a repurposed old fountain base, a modest stable structure built into the ground floor of a tower with straw and feed scattered nearby. This is infrastructure as ordinary as the market stalls beside it.

VERTICAL LIFE: residential levels rising above the market — balconies with laundry and plants, windows with warm interior light even in daytime shadow, narrow stairs and ramps connecting levels, the occasional rope bridge between buildings for a pedestrian shortcut.

LIGHT: warm morning sun, golden and low, filtering unevenly through the dense vertical structures — bright pools on the market street alternating with deep shadow in the narrow passages; strong dark/light/dark rhythm emerging from the density of the architecture itself, not from dramatic staging.

SHOW four views on one sheet:
VIEW 1 — THE MARKET STREET: a narrow street at foot level, stalls on both sides, awnings overhead nearly touching, civilians and a small dinosaur or two moving through, morning light breaking through gaps above.
VIEW 2 — THE COURTYARD: a wider gathering space where several streets meet, a communal watering trough/fountain repurposed for dinosaur use, laundry lines crossing overhead, residential balconies rising on all sides.
VIEW 3 — THE STABLE CORNER: a ground-floor structure built into an old tower base, a cargo hauler or courier dinosaur resting/tied, feed and tack hanging nearby, the ordinary infrastructure of dinosaur-as-transport.
VIEW 4 — VERTICAL LIFE: looking up from street level at the residential stack above the market — balconies, laundry, potted plants, warm window light, the vertical forest growing through gaps in the old structure.

Environment design sheet for THE STARTING PLAZA, from an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film.

Distinct from the finish line arena — this is the place of departure, not arrival: openness and multiplicity instead of a single sacred destination point. A vast circular plaza built into the remains of an ancient monumental square, ringed by tiered spectator structures, scaffolding, bridges and ruins capable of holding thousands.

DESIGN: unlike the finish arena's single unifying fabric arch, the starting plaza radiates OUTWARD — dozens of narrow avenues and passages branch away from the central grid in every direction, since the race has no fixed track, only a destination far across the city that each rider reaches by their own path. The ground itself is a wide worn stone grid, its surface polished smooth and marked with countless overlapping claw-prints and footprints layered from generations of starts. A tall wooden starting platform stands at the plaza's edge, hung with the current season's clan banners in bold saturated colors. Smaller personal pennants mark each racer's waiting position on the grid. Vegetation frames the plaza's edges, cascading down from the ringed structures. Morning light, long raking shadows, the golden hour of a festival dawn.

Environment design sheet for THE ACCIDENT SITE / THE MENDED BRIDGE, the emotional core location of an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film.

The place where the legendary champion duo crashed thirteen years ago — and where the race route crosses again today. CRITICAL: this sheet shows the PRESENT-DAY REPAIRED state — patched, mended, and structurally WHOLE, not broken. It must read as safely crossable at full racing speed.

DESIGN: a narrow pedestrian-scale stone bridge spanning a vertiginous ravine between two ancient city-canyon walls — intimate, built for one duo at a time. The original weathered stone flagstones, pale and sun-bleached, dominate most of the span — but at the exact point of the old collapse, a visibly MENDED section interrupts the pattern: newer cast concrete and cut stone, distinctly lighter and rawer in color/texture than the surrounding thirteen-year-old weathered original, dark welded metal support struts bracing the underside, a few replacement guardrail sections in slightly mismatched metal. This is honest, functional repair work — not a disguise. A visible SEAM where old stone meets new marks exactly where the break happened, a scar the bridge still carries, thematically echoing the riders' own repaired, scarred bodies. Moss and wild grass have begun to soften the edges of the repair, but the material contrast stays legible up close.

At the bridge's center, away from the repaired section, a wide still PUDDLE spans the walkway — a natural mirror holding the sky and the silhouette of anyone approaching, rippling faintly.

THE VOID BELOW: an immense vertical drop between two flanking canyon-walls of dense ancient towers — one side catching warm golden hazy light, the other falling into cool silhouette. Far at the bottom, a still body of water mirrors the entire city upside-down, doubling the skyline into an inverted reflection.

FLANKING CITY WALLS: dense vertical towers rising like canyon cliffs on both sides of the bridge, windows and floor-lines readable near the bridge, dissolving into soft atmospheric silhouettes with distance.

LIGHT: warm late-day golden haze, soft volumetric god-rays cutting through dust and mist, one side of the canyon walls lit warm gold, the other cool and shadowed — strong dark/light/dark separation.

SHOW four views on one sheet:
VIEW 1 — THE SIGNATURE APPROACH: straight down the walkway toward the far end, the puddle dominating the foreground, guardrails converging in perspective, the MENDED SECTION visible mid-span as a patch of distinctly different-colored stone — WHOLE and crossable, not broken.
VIEW 2 — FROM BELOW, LOOKING UP: camera low within the ravine looking up at the bridge's thin, structurally WHOLE silhouette crossing high overhead between the two canyon walls, the mirrored city and water visible far below.
VIEW 3 — THE REPAIR DETAIL: close view of the mended section mid-span — the visible seam where new stone meets old, welded support struts, mismatched guardrail metal, moss beginning to soften the edges of the newer material — a healed wound, not an open one.
VIEW 4 — GROUND TEXTURE: close-up of the original flagstone paving, moss-filled cracks, and the edge of the central puddle reflecting sky.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — Wren, a rookie about to race her first start, passes the open workshop and begs Kael to ride today. Before he can answer, Narek arrives mounted on Pyro and mocks him — "an old man and a broken lizard." Ashe nearly attacks. Kael holds him back, and speaks his only line in the entire film — not to Narek, but to Wren: "Win it for me." He never dignifies Narek with a response. That silence is more powerful than any comeback.
2. EMOTIONAL LAW — THE ECONOMY OF WORDS IS THE POINT. Wren is loud with hope; Narek is cutting and amused; Kael says four words in the whole film and they land like a verdict. His silence toward Narek is not weakness — it is a man who stopped needing to win arguments thirteen years ago. Ashe's fury is the emotion Kael won't let himself show.
3. KAEL'S PERFORMANCE — steady through the taunt, jaw tight but eyes calm; he does not even look at Narek when he speaks — he looks only at Wren. The half-smile when he says his line is the first real warmth we've seen from him since the fall.
4. ASHE'S PERFORMANCE — the moment his fury has a target: feathers snapping up along the neck, a full-body lunge half a step toward Narek and Pyro, a low guttural warning sound. Kael's hand closes hard on his neck/harness point — not a light touch, a real restraint. Ashe obeys, but his eyes stay locked on Narek as they leave.
5. NAREK'S PERFORMANCE — no real malice, just the careless cruelty of someone who has never lost. He barely looks at Kael when he says it — he's already looking past him, at Wren, mildly amused. This is the arrogance that costs him later.
6. WREN'S PERFORMANCE — unguarded excitement, no cynicism yet — she is everything Kael and Narek both used to be before either winning or losing changed them.
7. CAMERA LAW — organic handheld throughout, calibrated: warm and slightly unsteady on Wren's excitement; the camera goes LEVEL and unnervingly STILL the moment Narek speaks — stillness as menace; a sharp handheld JOLT on Ashe's lunge, breaking the calm violently for one beat; settled and calm again on Kael's line — his stillness is the answer to Narek's stillness, but warmer. ONE Ashe POV insert on the lunge.
8. COMPOSITION LAW — by thirds, never centered. SCALE LAW applies to BOTH pairs in frame: Ashe (2.5m/5.5m) towers over Kael (1.80m) exactly as established; Pyro, even compact, must read taller at the shoulder than Narek's own head. When both duos share a wide shot, neither pair should ever be mistaken for equal in scale to the other — Ashe and Pyro are comparable giants, their riders comparably dwarfed. Narek and Pyro should be framed from a slightly LOW angle on arrival — looming, unearned confidence made visual.
9. LIGHT — the same morning light as the rest of the workshop scenes: one hard diagonal shaft near the doorway where Wren stands, warm and open; Narek and Pyro arrive from the brighter exterior, briefly silhouetted black against the outside light before resolving into color — an entrance that reads as an intrusion. Kael and Ashe remain inside the workshop's deeper shadow throughout, contrasted against the light at the door.

Full creature character design sheet for PYRO, the racing dinosaur of the current champion, from an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film.

PYRO is a large adult feathered racing dromaeosaur at the peak of his career — powerful, disciplined, obedient, flawlessly trained. He is the living contrast to the protagonist's dinosaur: where Ashe is warm-eyed and guarded despite his scars, PYRO is physically formidable and hard-featured — a genuinely intimidating animal held in total leashed control by his rider's command. His BEHAVIOR is composed and disciplined (excellence through training, not chaos), but his BUILT-IN APPEARANCE — bone structure, musculature, the set of his eyes — reads as fierce and dangerous even at rest, distinct from Ashe's more approachable design language.

BODY DESIGN — AGGRESSIVELY GRAPHIC, NON-REALISTIC ANATOMY, NOTICEABLY MORE POWERFUL AND MASSIVE THAN ASHE: a deliberately different build from a long arrow-like racer — PYRO is more COMPACT, EXPLOSIVE and heavily muscled, a sprinter built like a coiled weapon. The whole body reads as a dense coiled wedge, even bulkier and more armored-looking than before. Skull LARGE, heavy and angular, built from hard cut planes with pronounced brow ridges casting the eyes into shadow — a naturally severe, scowling structure even in a neutral pose. Chest exceptionally deep, wide and overbuilt, a faceted power block noticeably broader than Ashe's leaner frame. Shorter, thicker, more muscular neck. Waist narrow, exaggerating the power of the chest and legs by contrast. Legs massive, thick and long, built from stacked angular planes and heavy visible muscle striation — the most powerful, intimidating legs of any racing dinosaur in the film. Large blocky clawed feet, the claws slightly more pronounced and visible than other racing mounts. Tail slightly shorter and thicker than a typical dromaeosaur, carried as one rigid graphic diagonal, giving an impression of coiled aggression even when still.

HEAD — DELIBERATELY FIERCE AND HARD-FEATURED, DISTINCT FROM ASHE'S DESIGN: large wedge-shaped skull, heavy angular jaw with a pronounced, slightly undershot power to it, hinting at visible sharp teeth even with the mouth closed. Low, heavy, downward-angled brow ridge casting a permanent hard, severe expression — a look that reads as dangerous and intimidating even at rest, the opposite of soft or friendly. Eyes narrow, sharp and cold rather than warm or approachable — a hard predatory stare, small and piercing, deliberately less "intelligent and gentle-reading" than Ashe's eyes and more unsettling. Clean unscarred muzzle — a career without accidents — but the structure of the face itself should read as naturally mean and formidable regardless of the absence of scars, through bone structure and expression alone, not damage. This is a face that looks like trouble even when its owner is behaving perfectly.

FEATHERS: short primitive feathers with larger graphic feather masses as sculpted wedges and painterly brush shapes — NO individual photorealistic feathers. A trimmed, groomed crest of swept-back feathers behind the skull — visibly maintained by human hands, contrasting the wilder feathering of other animals. Tail ending in compact directional feather blocks.

RACING GEAR: pristine champion racing saddle and low-profile harness — matte dark metal connection points, structured woven tension straps in emerald and vermillion, leather grip surfaces, small gold champion cords. Immaculate condition, perfectly fitted, allowing full shoulder freedom.

COLOR DESIGN: primary body deep red-black / dark crimson; secondary feather masses intense vermillion and deep burgundy; underside dark warm gray; small bold GOLD markings around the eyes and along the neck. Deep crimson shadows rather than neutral gray. Vibrant, sophisticated, instantly distinguishable from any teal/turquoise animal at any distance.

Full character design sheet for YOUNG KAEL, the protagonist of an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film, shown at the peak of his racing career.

KAEL is a 30-year-old legendary dinosaur racing champion — the greatest rider his world has ever seen. Confident to the edge of arrogance. Undefeated. Worshipped by crowds.

PERSONALITY THROUGH DESIGN: absolute confidence, controlled aggression, pride, physical precision, a man who has never lost anything in his life. His posture is upright, chin slightly raised, shoulders open — he owns every space he enters.

BODY SHAPE — AGGRESSIVELY EXAGGERATED, NON-REALISTIC: his proportions must look deliberately wrong by realistic standards. Head clearly TOO SMALL for his height. Shoulders wide and angular. Torso an elongated inclined trapezoid. Waist too narrow. Arms and legs TOO LONG. Hands clearly TOO LARGE. Feet large and blocky. Neck long and strongly marked. Environment design sheet for FOUR NEW STRETCHES of THE RACE CIRCUIT, from an original mature painterly paleo-futuristic animated film. Same reclaimed-brutalism monumental architecture established throughout the world, same city, different specific locations along the racing route not yet designed. POST-APOCALYPTIC BUT ALIVE: bare weathered concrete is the base, but every view must show nature aggressively reclaiming it — thick vines, root systems splitting facades, moss and lichen mapping the surfaces, flowering plants, small trees growing through cracks and windows — plus BOLD SATURATED COLOR from the world's established fabric/banner language (turquoise, coral, saffron, violet — woven canopies, banners, rigging ropes) providing deliberate chromatic contrast against the grey "stone jungle" of the ruins. SHOW four views on one sheet:

Thick vines and root systems cascade down both walls, moss and small ferns growing in every crack, a few flowering vines in saturated coral and violet breaking up the grey stone. Midway along the passage, one section of the floor slab has fractured and partially collapsed at the outer edge: a jagged broken lip of concrete and exposed rebar, hanging out over a sheer drop into deep shadow between the towers' bases far below — a fall here is not survivable without intervention. The passage floor elsewhere is intact and racing-solid. Weak light filters down from a narrow gap of sky directly overhead, leaving the passage itself in cool, tense half-shadow — a stark contrast to the warm open avenues elsewhere on the route. Support cables and one broken rope bridge fragment hang uselessly from the passage's upper walls, remnants of an older crossing, a few tattered scraps of turquoise fabric still clinging to the rigging.

Rooftop gardens gone wild — dense green overgrowth, small trees, flowering plants in saturated color spilling over ledges — alongside laundry lines strung with saffron and coral fabric catching the wind, a few patched banner-canopies still standing between structures. Old rail tracks embedded and half-buried in the floor, condensation and moss on the curved walls, a sense of compressed speed and darkness between light.
